claims.text: Agent 365 is an enterprise control plane for observing, governing, and securing AI agents.
claims.qualification: Capabilities depend on integration, configuration, permissions, and licensing.

claims.text: The Agent 365 SDK extends an existing agent; it does not build, host, deploy, orchestrate, or execute the agent.
claims.locator: What it is and what it isn't
claims.qualification: The separate Agent 365 CLI has deployment functions; do not confuse SDK and CLI responsibilities.

claims.text: Agent 365 SDK complements, rather than replaces, the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK.
claims.locator: How is the Agent 365 SDK different? / Compare Microsoft Agent 365 SDK and Microsoft 365 Agents SDK

S02: How is the Agent 365 SDK different?
S05: Compare Microsoft Agent 365 SDK and Microsoft 365 Agents SDK

claims.qualification: The Microsoft 365 Agents SDK remains a conversational-agent framework.

claims.text: The developer SDK adds identity, observability, tooling, and notifications as selectable capabilities.
claims.qualification: Adopt only capabilities required by the scenario; not every agent needs the entire SDK.

claims.text: Check built-in integration and registry synchronization before adding SDK code only for registration.
claims.qualification: Registry sync is preview and only applies to supported connected platforms. Do not infer it is a Copilot Studio fallback. Built-in platform coverage and administrative enablement vary.

claims.text: The identity model distinguishes a blueprint, an agent identity, and an optional agent user account.
claims.qualification: Blueprint credentials are shared across derived identities; not every agent uses a user account.

claims.text: S2S acts as the agent without human user context; OBO acts for a signed-in user; Agentic-User acts as the agent's own user account.
claims.qualification: Confirm the downstream resource's permission and consent requirements. Agentic-User requires Frontier.

claims.text: An agent user account and notifications require the Frontier preview program.
claims.locator: Add messaging and notifications / What the SDK adds / Agent's user account
claims.qualification: Do not promise every agent a mailbox, Teams presence, or notifications.

claims.text: Work IQ MCP is in preview and requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and appropriate delegated permissions and administrator consent.
claims.qualification: The documented onboarding flow skips Work IQ tooling for S2S; do not infer application-only support.

claims.text: Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro is the recommended observability path for new integrations; the earlier Observability SDK continues to work.
claims.qualification: This recommendation concerns observability, not replacement of all Agent 365 SDK capabilities.

claims.text: Telemetry needs a valid invoke_agent root span for the main agent-activity surfaces, with tool and inference spans correlated underneath.
claims.locator: Instrument for observability / Where Agent 365 observability data appears
claims.qualification: Without the root, child spans can still be queryable in Defender advanced hunting; do not say all telemetry is lost.

claims.text: Observability requires at least one user assigned an Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7 license; a tenant SKU alone is insufficient.
claims.qualification: The licensed user need not be the caller. An HTTP 200 is not proof of accepted ingestion.

claims.text: For direct OTel ingestion, the route agent ID and gen_ai.agent.id must match the authenticated agent appId.
claims.locator: Agent identity is bound to the URL
claims.qualification: Do not substitute an Entra object ID or blueprint appId. SDK/Distro abstract wire-level routing.

claims.text: Microsoft Entra, Purview, and Defender provide identity, data/compliance, and threat-defense controls in the Agent 365 ecosystem.
claims.qualification: These are configured capabilities, not a universal guarantee against leakage or malicious actions.

claims.text: Agent 365 became generally available for the Commercial segment on May 1, 2026, with per-user licensing.
claims.qualification: Feature-level preview and GCC differences remain; GA does not imply universal feature availability.

claims.text: Basic inventory and governance availability differs from licensed advanced monitoring, policy, tool, and API features.
claims.qualification: Use the current service-description matrix and tenant entitlements; this pack does not determine a customer's license.

claims.text: Declaring blueprint permissions does not grant them; administrator consent is required.
claims.qualification: Azure RBAC roles are assigned directly to agent identities, not blueprints.

claims.text: The standard onboarding pattern is register, extend, validate, and operate.
claims.qualification: Agent 365 Skills can guide setup, but tenant, Azure, role, and capability prerequisites must be checked.

claims.text: On native Windows, the Microsoft-managed Agent 365 CLI application uses WAM; policy-blocked device code is not a reason to disable security controls.
claims.locator: Microsoft Entra authentication / Device code authentication is blocked
claims.qualification: Managed app availability is staged; tenant-owned custom applications use a different supported authentication path.
